title: Narada briefs Valmiki about Rama and the Ramayana in a nutshell
introduction: Divine sage Narada arrives at the hermitage of Sage Valmiki in order to enlighten him and keep him informed of his duty to author the epic poem Ramayana. In the dialogue between these two sages, Valmiki elicits from Narada about most virtuous person on earth, namely Rama. In this opening chapter, while eulogizing Rama Narada gives an outline of Ramayana, truly highlighting those aspects that are the keynotes in this epic, like virtuosity, generosity, morality, chastity and the like.

Valmiki Ramayana is said to have been composed basing on each of the twenty-four letters of Gayatri Hymn, and a thousand verses are arranged into one book under the caption of each letter. Though that classification, or dividing verses into thousand chapters is unavailable now, the twenty-four verses identified with the 24 letters of Gayatri hymn, called as Gayatri Ramayana, is available and it is given in the endnote of this page. In tune with the scheme of Gayatri, Ramayana starts the first verse with letter ta an auspicious letter.
closing: Thitherto, the Bala Kanda is narrated by these narrations of sparkled in Ikshvaku dynasty 'Rama's incarnation...' highly valorous, enemy subjugator... 'elimination of demoness Tataka, subdual of the vanity of Parashu Rama...' propitious 'marriage with Seetha, knows Art of Archery 'receiving missiles from Vishvamitra...' From now poet tells the Ayodhya Kanda, and a gist of this magnum opus is given here itself. This narration is known as bāla rāmayana - saṅkṣepa rāmāyaṇa meaning that it is aimed at youngsters as it has been told in an abridged version. In the endnote, details about this version and still abridged version, called Gayatri Ramayana, are given.

श्लोकेन प्रति साहस्रं प्रथमे क्रमात् |
गायत्र्यक्षरमेकैकं स्थापयामास वै मुनिः ||

१. त -
तपः स्वाध्यायनिरतं तपस्वी वाग्विदां वरम् |
नारदं परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुङ्गवम् || १-१-१
२. स -
स हत्वा राक्षसान् सर्वान् यज्ञघ्नान् रघुनन्दनः |
ऋषिभिः पूजितस्तत्र यथेन्द्रो विजये पुरा || १-३०-२४
३. वि -
विश्वामित्रस्तु धर्मात्मा श्रुत्वा जनकभाषितम् |
वत्स राम धनुः पश्य इति राघवमब्रवीत् || १-६७-१२ - बालकाण्डम्
४. तु -
तुष्टावास्य तदा वंशं प्रविश्य स विशांपतेः |
शयनीयं नरेन्द्रस्य तदासाद्य व्यतिष्ठत || २-१५-२०
५. व -
वनवासं हि संख्याय वासांस्याभरणानि च |
 भर्तारमनुगच्छन्त्यै सीतायै श्वशुरो ददौ || २-४०-१५
६. रा -
राजा सत्यञ्च धर्मश्च राजा कुलवतां कुलम् |
राजा माता पिता चैव राजा हितकरो नृणाम् || २-६७-३४
७. नि -
निरीक्ष्य स मुहूर्तं तु ददर्श भरतो गुरुम् |
उटजे राममासीनं जटामण्डलधारिणम् || २-९९-२५ - अयोध्याकाण्डम्
 ८. य -
यदि बुद्धिः कृता द्रष्टुमगस्त्यं तं महामुनिम् |
अद्यैव गमने बुद्धिं रोचयस्व महायशः || ३-११-४५
 ९. भ -
भरतस्यार्यपुत्रस्य श्वश्रूणां मम च प्रभो |
मृगरूपमिदं व्यक्तं विस्मयं जनयिष्यति || ३-४३-१७
१०. ग -
गच्छ शीघ्रमितो राम सुग्रीवं तं महाबलम् |
वयस्यं तं कुरु क्षिप्रमितो गत्वाद्य राघव || ३-७२-१७ - अरण्यकाण्डम्
 ११. दे -
देशकालौ प्रतीक्षस्व क्षममाणः प्रियाप्रिये |
सुखदुःखसहः काले सुग्रीववशगो भव || ४-२२-१९
१२. व -
वन्द्यास्ते तु तपः सिद्ध सप्तसा वीतकल्मषाः |
प्रष्टव्या चापि सीतायाः प्रवृत्तिर्विनयान्वितैः || ४-४३-३४ - किष्किन्धाकाण्डम्
१३. स -
 स निर्जित्य पुरीं श्रेष्ठां लङ्का तां कामरूपिणीम् |
विक्रमेण महातेजा हनूमान् कपिसत्तमः || ५-४-१
 १४. ध -
धन्या देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः |
मम पश्यन्ति ये नाथं रामं राजीवलोचनम् || ५-२६-४१
१५. म -
मङ्गलाभिमुखी तस्य सा तदासीन्महाकपेः |
उपतस्थे विशालाक्षी प्रयता हव्यवाहनम् || ५-५३-२८ - सुन्दरकाण्डम्
१६. हि -
हितं महार्थं मृदु हेतुसंहितम्
व्यतीतकालायति सम्प्रति क्षमम् |
निशम्य तद्वाक्यमुपास्थितज्वरः
प्रसङ्गवानुत्तरमेतदब्रवीत् || ६-१०-२७
१७. ध -
धर्मात्मा रक्षसां श्रेष्ठः सम्प्राप्तोऽयं विभीषणः |
लङ्कैश्वर्यं ध्रुवं श्रीमानयं प्राप्नोत्यकण्टकम् || ६-४१-६९
 १८. यो -
यो वज्रपाताशनिसन्निपातान्
न चुक्षुभे नापि चचाल राजा |
 स रामबाणाभिहतो भृशार्तः
चचाल चापं च मुमोच वीरः || ६-५९-१३९
१९. य -
यस्य विक्रममासाद्य राक्षसा निधनं गताः |
तं मन्ये राघवं वीरं नारायणमनामयम् || ६-७२-११
२०. न -
न ते ददृशिरे रामं दहन्तमरिवाहिनीम् |
मोहिताः परमास्त्रेण गान्धर्वेण महात्मना || ६-९४-२६
२१. प्र -
प्रणम्य देवताभ्यश्च ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च मैथिली |
बद्धाञ्जलिपुटा चेदमुवाचाग्निसमीपतः || ६-११९-२३ - युद्धकाण्डम्
 २२. च -
चालनात् पर्वतस्यैव गणा देवस्य कम्पिताः |
चचाल पार्वती चापि तदाश्लिष्टा महेश्वरम् || ७-१६-२६
२३. द -
दाराः पुत्राः पुरं राष्ट्रं भोगाच्छादनभोजनम् |
सर्वमेवाविभक्तं नो भविष्यति हरीश्वर || ७-३४-४१
२४. य -
यामेव रात्रिं शत्रुघ्नः पर्णशालां समाविशत् |
तामेव रात्रिं सीतापि प्रसूता दारकद्वयम् || ७-६६-१ - उत्तरकाण्डम्

इदं रामायणं कृत्स्नं गायत्रीबीजसंयुतम् |
त्रिसन्ध्यं यः पठेन्नित्यं सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ||

यावदावर्तते चक्रं यावती च वसुन्धरा |
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि स्वामित्वमवधारय ||
मङ्गलं कोसलेन्द्राय महनीयगुणात्मने |
चक्रवर्ति तनूजाय सार्वभौमाय मङ्गलम् ||

इति गायत्री रामायणं सम्पूर्णम्
इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे प्रथमः सर्गः ||
Thus, this is the 1st chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
तपःस्वाध्यायनिरतं तपस्वी वाग्विदां वरम् |
नारदं परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुङ्गवम् ||
verses.iast:
tapaḥ svādhyāya niratām tapasvī vāgvidām varam |
nāradam paripapraccha vālmīkiḥ muni puṅgavam ||
verses.translation: The ascetic Valmiki inquired Naarada - 'who engaged deeply in austerity and study of Vedas, best among the eloquent and eminent among sages' (as follows:).
notes: The epic starts with the word auspicious word ta as said in 'takārovighnanāśakaḥ', 'takārosaukhyadāyakaḥ'...

glosses.meaning: deeply engaged in austerity and study of Vedas

verses.devanagari:
को न्वस्मिन् साम्प्रतं लोके गुणवान् कश्च वीर्यवान् |
धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सत्यवाक्यो दृढव्रतः ||
verses.iast:
kaḥ nu asmin sāmpratam loke guṇavān kaḥ ca vīryavān |
dharmajñaḥ ca kṛtajñaḥ ca satya vākyo dhṛḍha vrataḥ ||
verses.translation: "Who really is that person in this present world, who is virtuous and vigorous, a conscientious one, one who is mindful of good deeds done to him, and also a speaker of truth and who is determined in his deed...

glosses.meaning: one who is mindful of good deeds done to him also

verses.devanagari:
चारित्रेण च को युक्तः सर्वभूतेषु को हितः |
विद्वान् कः कः समर्थश्च कश्चैकप्रियदर्शनः ||
verses.translation: "Who is appropriate in disposition... who is interested in welfare of all beings... who is adept and also an able one... also uniquely pleasant to look at...
notes: The adeptness of that person is in his knowing all the knowable aspects in this world, and he must be able to retain that knowledge to translate into his deeds, not just to sit back with his bookish knowledge, but with utmost practicality. His conduct-wise character shall be acceptable i.e., by his lineage he shall be noble, by his education he must be well-read, by his actions they must be conducive to norms laid down in Veda-s, and thus given any area, he should conduct himself properly. And he must be benign not only to higher-ups but to lowly subjects, like Guha, Shabari et al., and he should deal with wrongdoers and right-doers conscientiously. Further, he in his mien he shall be pleasant, but not an unsightly one. The word eka also means 'unique' and thus his complexion, facial, physical structures etc., shall be unique and shall differ from ordinary beings. kṣaṇe kṣaṇe yat navatām upaiti tadeva rūpam ramaṇīyatāyāḥ 'which / what / who gets newness moment by moment, that alone is pleasant...'

glosses.meaning: who is interested in welfare of all beings
who is also uniquely pleasant to look at.

verses.devanagari:
आत्मवान् को जितक्रोधो द्युतिमान् कोऽनसूयकः |
कस्य बिभ्यति देवाश्च जातरोषस्य संयुगे ||
verses.iast:
ātmavān ko jitakrodho dyutimān kaḥ anasūyakaḥ |
kasya bibhyati devāḥ ca jāta roṣasya saṃyuge ||
verses.translation: "Who is that self-composed one, who controlled his ire, who is brilliant, non-jealous and whom do even the gods fear, when provoked to war...

verses.devanagari:
एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं परं कौतूहलं हि मे |
महर्षे त्वं समर्थोऽसि ज्ञातुमेवंविधं नरम् ||
verses.iast:
etat icchāmi aham śrotum param kautūhalam hi me |
maharṣe tvam samartho'si jñātum evam vidham naram ||
verses.translation: "All this I wish to listen from you, oh! Great Sage, you are competent to know this kind of man, and indeed my inquisitiveness is immense..." Thus Valmiki enquired with Narada.
notes: Valmiki wanted to know about that man - a man with godly qualities. Valmiki is thinking aloud, about the qualities of his prospective hero of this epic and these are the very opening questions put to an Omniscient Sage Narada. Both the sages know of Rama and his deeds. Even then Valmiki asks Narada, "who is that man with godly qualities?' If Narada tells that Rama is Vishnu Himself, there is nothing left for Valmiki to compose his epic, because there are numerous mythologies, puraaNa-s, that have already adored God Vishnu. If Narada tells that Rama is so-and-so king, again Valmiki need not attempt to author about some king, however great that king might be.

The attributes of the hero of Ramayana, as required by Valmiki, are 16; sixteen in number.1 - guṇavān 2 - viryavān 3 - dharmajñaḥ 4 - kṛtajñaḥ 5 - satyavākyaḥ 6 - dhṛḍhavrataḥ 7 - cāritravān 8 - sarvabhūteṣu hitaḥ 9 - vidvān 10 - samarthaḥ - 11 - priyadarśanaḥ 12 - ātmavān 13 - jitakrodhaḥ 14 - dyutimān 15 - anasūyakaḥ 16 - bibhyatidevāḥ These sixteen attributes are attributed to the sixteen phases of the Full Moon, and Valmiki is about to picture Rama to be as pleasant as a full-moon.

glosses.meaning: all this I wish to listen

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा चैतत्त्रिलोकज्ञो वाल्मीकेर्नारदो वचः |
श्रूयतामिति चामन्त्र्य प्रहृष्टो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ||
verses.iast:
śrutvā ca etat trilokajño vālmīkeḥ nārado vacaḥ |
śrūyatām iti ca āmantrya prahṛṣṭo vākyam abravīt ||
verses.translation: On listening all those words of Valmiki, Narada, the knower of all the three worlds, said "let it be heard..." and beckoning at Sage Valmiki to listen attentively, he spoke these words very gladly.
notes: Narada is cognizant of three worlds, where the three worlds are bhūloka, bhuvarloka, suvarloka this world, the intermediary heaven, the heavens themselves.

glosses.meaning: on listening to all those words

verses.devanagari:
बहवो दुर्लभाश्चैव ये त्वया कीर्तिता गुणाः |
मुने वक्ष्याम्यहं बुद्ध्वा तैर्युक्तः श्रूयतां नरः ||
verses.iast:
bahavo durlabhāḥ ca eva ye tvayā kīrtitā guṇāḥ |
mune vaxṣyāmi aham buddhvā taiḥ uktaḥ śrūyatām naraḥ ||
verses.translation: "Oh! Sage Valmiki, the merits which you have extolled are many, and unattainable. I, after having known from Brahma of such a man with all these merits, will speak on...Let it be heard." Thus Narada started to say.
notes: Narada came hither to impart the legend of Rama, as Brahma already imparted the same to him, and wanted him to impart these very attributes to Valmiki to compose Ramayana. It is a coincidence of interests Valmiki and those of Narada and Brahma.

verses.devanagari:
इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः |
नियतात्मा महावीर्यो द्युतिमान् धृतिमान् वशी ||
verses.iast:
ikṣvāku vaṃśa prabhavo rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ |
niyata ātmā mahāvīryo dyutimān dhṛtimān vaśī ||
verses.translation: "One emerged from Ikshvaku dynasty, known to people as Rama by name. He is with a controlled self, highly valorous, resplendent, steadfast and a controller of (vice and vile... or) his own senses.
notes: For the attributes explained by Narada there are some Vedanta imports. From niyatātmā to vaśī these are the attributes of the Supreme Being, Absolute of Brahman. svarūpa-nirūpaka- lakṣaṇāḥ . This niyatātmā is 'immutable Absolute, this is the postulate of any Upanishad: ya ātmā apahatapāpmā virajo vimṛtyurviśoko... 8-7-1, Chāndogya-UpaniShad. mahāvīryaḥ = acintya vividhavicitraśaktivān Absolute is Omnicompetent parā asya śaktiḥ vividhā iva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñānabalakriyā ca 6-8, Shwetaashvatara-UpaniShad. The word dyutimān is for the attribute of Self-Resplendent Absolute, or, Resplendence of Consciousness. tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvam tasya bhāsā sarvam idam bhāti 2-11, Mundaka-UpaniShad. And the dhṛthimān is Sublime Bliss, according to Vyjayanti dhṛtiḥ tu tuṣṭiḥ santoṣaḥ and as said in ānando brahma - ānandāt eva khalu imāni bhūtāni jāyante 6, Taittariiya- Upanishad. Next, vaśī Absolute is the Omnipotent on the entire Universe. eko vahī sarva bhūtāntarātmā 2-5-12, Katha-Upanishad and sarvasya vaśī sarvasya īśānaḥ and the like. The rest of the attributes of Rama as said by Narada are identifiable with the causative factors of that Absolute in Creation, and the process of Creation is the self-expression of the Absolute.

verses.devanagari:
बुद्धिमान्नीतिमान्वाग्ग्मी श्रीमान् शत्रुनिबर्हणः |
विपुलांसो महाबाहुः कम्बुग्रीवो महाहनुः ||
verses.iast:
buddhimān nītimān vāñgmī śrīmān śatru nibarhaṇaḥ |
vipulāṃso mahābāhuḥ kambu grīvo mahāhanuḥ ||
verses.translation: "He is a wise one, moralist, eloquent, glorious, and a destroyer of enemies. His arms are lengthy, with three lines in the neck [indicative of good fortune], and cheekbones high...
notes: The Absolute is an adept one in creating the Creation yat sarvajñaḥ sarvavit. He is nītimān one who maintains the rhythm of universe as said at eṣa setuḥ vidharaṇa eṣām lokanāmasambhedāya... He is propitious because śrīḥ kāntisampadoḥ lakśmyām... gleaming, glistering richness of prosperity emanates from him. The following stanzas describe the physical qualities an Emperor should have by birth, as per sāmudrikaśāstra, the physiognomic treatise of astrology.

glosses.meaning: with three lines in the neck [indicative of good fortune]

verses.devanagari:
महोरस्को महेष्वासो गूढजत्रुररिन्दमः |
आजानुबाहुः सुशिराः सुललाटः सुविक्रमः ||
verses.iast:
mahorasko maheṣvāso gūḍha jatruḥ arindamaḥ |
ājānu bāhuḥ suśirāḥ sulalāṭaḥ suvikramaḥ ||
verses.translation: "He is lion-chested, with concealed collarbones, knee-length are his arms, and his is a long bow, an enemy-subjugator, and his emperor's countenance is with a crowning-head and an ample forehead, and his gait is majestic like that of a lion...
notes: When his physique is extolled, suddenly a weapon is said, in saying that 'his is longbow...' this is called prakramabhangadoṣa 'jump-cut in narration...' It is not so, his lengthy arms are said firstly and those arms can wield a great bow that can eliminate enemies, both physical and psychological ones like ariṣaḍvarga like desire, ire, avarice, conceit etc., as detailed in verse 4 above.

verses.devanagari:
समः समविभक्ताङ्गः स्निग्धवर्णः प्रतापवान् |
पीनवक्षा विशालाक्षो लक्ष्मीवान् शुभलक्षणः ||
verses.iast:
samaḥ sama vibhakta aṅgaḥ snigdha varṇaḥ pratāpavān |
pīna vakṣā viśālākṣo lakṣmīvān śubha lakṣaṇaḥ ||
verses.translation: "He is built proportionately physically, with limbs poised symmetrically, sinew-chested, wide-eyed, complexioned charmingly... he is a prosperous one with all the auspicious features ...
notes: Up to here the godly physical aspect bhagavadvigraha is explained that which is perceptible by the adherents as said in Chāndogya Upanishad: ya eṣo antarāditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣo dṛśyate... 1-6-6. From now on, the features that are reliable for the adherers are said.

verses.devanagari:
धर्मज्ञः सत्यसन्धश्च प्रजानां च हिते रतः |
यशस्वी ज्ञानसंपन्नः शुचिर्वश्यः समाधिमान् ||
verses.iast:
dharmajñaḥ satya sandhaḥ ca prajānām ca hite rataḥ |
yaśasvī jñāna sampannaḥ śuciḥ vaśyaḥ samādhimān ||
verses.translation: "He is the knower of rectitude, bidden by the truth, also his concern is in the welfare of subjects, proficient in prudence, clean in his conduct, self-controlled and an attentive one...

glosses.meaning: also concerned in welfare of subjects

verses.devanagari:
प्रजापतिसमः श्रीमान् धाता रिपुनिषूदनः |
रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य धर्मस्य परिरक्षिता||
verses.iast:
prajāpati samaḥ śrīmān dhātā ripu niṣUdanaḥ |
rakśitā jīvalokasya dharmasya pari rakśitā ||
verses.translation: "He equals Lord Vishnu, the Lord of all creatures, Sustainer of the Universe, together with Sri Lakshmi (shriimaan = lakShmiivaan), Eliminator of enemies, Protector of the world of living creatures and complete Guardian of probity...
notes:
The word रक्षिता is the Nominative Singular of रक्षितृ and means Protector. Please note that prajaapatiH can be applied to Vedic Gods as well as to Lord Brahma, Lord Vishnu and Lord Maheswara. Here we consider Rama as equalling the Supreme God Lord Vishnu who is the One with Goddess Sri Lakshmi and also the sustainer. prajaapatiH is thus being translated as Lord Vishnu. Please note that we are deviating from traditional translations of prajaapatiH as Lord Brahma here and this is intentional.
 'These features show the aspects of Rama's incarnation...' Govindaraja. 'These features are available only in the Supreme Person, but unobtainable in any other...' Maheshvara Tiirtha. These two, Govindaraja and Maheshvara Tiirtha are reputed commentators on Ramayana among many others.

glosses.meaning: Protector of the world of living creatures

verses.devanagari:
रक्षिता स्वस्य धर्मस्य स्वजनस्य च रक्षिता |
वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञो धनुर्वेदे च निष्ठितः ||
verses.iast:
rakṣitā svasya dharmasya sva janasya ca rakṣitā |
veda vedāñga tattvajño dhanur vede ca niṣṭhitaḥ ||
verses.translation: "He is the preserver of his own righteousness and also a champion for adherent's welfare in the same righteousness, and he is a scholar in the essence of Veda-s and their ancillaries, too. He is an expert in dhanurVeda, the Art of Archery...
notes: These are the ancillary subjects of Vedas called anga part and upa-anga sub-part. The main parts of Veda-s are śikṣā ritual rigor vyākaraṇa grammar candas prosody jyotiśya astrology nirukta recital rules kalpa procedure rules. This apart, the dhanurveda science of archery, itself is treated as 'an exclusive Veda taught to warriors...' The dhanurveda is not to be construed as simple bow and arrow and 'shooting the target' education. It is a 'scripture on missiles' that existed in those ages.

Down the memory lane, O. A.Vijayan, the eminent Indian journalist has reflected in The Illustrated Weekly of India, that the Soviet scholar Dr. A. A. Gorbovsky said in his article with heading Ancient India may have had N-arms , in the Statesman, with dateline Moscow, Sept. 8, 1986. Among other things, the scientist observes by the stanzas that describe the disaster caused by such astra-s, now loosely termed as a well crafted bow and sky rocketing arrows, as below:

'A blazing shaft which possessed all the effulgence of smokeless fire was let off... all directions were enveloped by darkness... the very elements seemed to be perturbed... the sun seemed to turn... the universe, scorched with heat, seemed to be in fever... the survivors lost their hair and nails... for years the sun and sky remained shrouded with clouds...'

Thus the narration goes on. This is the account of Brahmaastra, as in Mahabharata, the other Epic of India. Thus the Dhanurveda may be taken as the canon of missile sciences, which fortunately has not been handed over to the successive generations, lest everything would have been annihilated by now. In Ramayana too, which is much earlier to Mahabharata, there are elaborate accounts of such astra-s in the coming chapters. Sage Vishvamitra, who is well-versed in warfare, gives many such weapons to Rama. For now, these bow and arrow references may not be taken as those of Robin Hood.

glosses.meaning: champion of his own people also

verses.devanagari:
सर्वशास्त्रार्थतत्त्वज्ञः स्मृतिमान् प्रतिभानवान् |
सर्वलोकप्रियः साधुरदीनात्मा विचक्षणः ||
verses.iast:
sarvaśāstrārthatattvajño smṛtimān pratibhānavān |
sarvaloka priyaḥ sādhuḥ adīnāatmā vicakṣaṇaḥ ||
verses.translation: "He is the knower of the meaning and essence of all the scriptures, excellent at memory, a brilliant one, and dear to all the worlds, gentle, level-headed and clear-headed in discriminating and distinguishing...

glosses.meaning: cognizant of the essence and meaning of all the scriptures
undepressed in spirit [level-headed even in severe trouble]

verses.devanagari:
सर्वदाभिगतः सद्भिः समुद्र इव सिन्धुभिः |
आर्यः सर्वसमश्चैव सदैव प्रियदर्शनः ||
verses.iast:
sarvadā abhigataḥ sadbhiḥ samudra iva sindhubhiḥ |
aryaḥ sarvasamaḥ ca eva sadaiva priya darśanaḥ ||
verses.translation: "Like an ocean that is reached by rivers, that reverential one too is always accessible and reachable by clean-minded ones, and he treats all equally, and ever a feast to eye...
notes: Here it is said 'he is reachable by all clean-minded ones...' satpravartana, sadbudhhi... and those that approach him with a sacrilegious intent, will meet their end at his hand. sarvasamaḥ means, that he does not discriminate people by their caste, creed, or by that individual's philosophy etc., like tribal boatman Guha, low-birthed Shabari, and nihilist Sage Jaabaali et al. jāti-guṇa- vṛtti-ādi bhedābhāvāt And the word eva in sa eva priyadarśanaḥ indicates 'always...' 'unvarying in his demeanour with anyone...' Govindaraja. And by the simile of ocean to Rama, for rivers there is no other course except an ocean; thus, the living beings, may it be humans or birds like Jataayu, have no other recourse than Rama.

glosses.meaning: indeed ever a feast to the eye.

verses.devanagari:
स च सर्वगुणोपेतः कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः |
समुद्र इव गाम्भीर्ये धैर्येण हिमवानिव ||
verses.iast:
sa ca sarva guṇopetaḥ kausalya ānanda vardhanaḥ |
samudra iva gāmbhīrye dhairyeṇa himavān iva ||
verses.translation: "He who betters the happiness of his mother Kausalya is an embodiment of all noble merits, and in profundity he is like an unfathomable ocean, and by fortitude he is unalterable like the kingly Himalayan mountain...
notes: At times Rama is said to be 'the son of Kausalya...' than the son of Dasharatha, because the word Kausalya does not signify his mother alone, the daughter of King of Kosala, but it has meanings like kṣema, kuśala, sāmarthya, puṇya, nipuṇatva 'safeness, soundness, capability, merit, expertise...' and this also signifies Queen Kausalya's worshipping of Vishnu. When dynasty, valour, braveness etc., are said, Rama's name will be attached with Dasharatha. An ocean is not a bottomless one but an unfathomable one. So also Rama's heart has a reachable bottom, where pearls, gems, and other treasures of virtues are abounding, and it can be reached with a heartily approach. For a hard-hearted one, Rama's heart becomes an unfathomable abyss and he will get lost in it. girayoḥ varṣadhārābhirharyamāṇā na vivyadhuḥ | abhibhūyamānā vyasanaiḥ yathā adhokṣajacetasā || 'true devotees do not get hassled though subjected to many problems, for they place their faith in the Supreme. Equally, mountains are unshaken though battered by storms or lightings...' So, like a mountain he is unalterable and constant for a true devotee. An icy-mountain is meltable by scorching sun, thus Rama also melts down when his adherents are scorched with their problems.

glosses.meaning: One who betters Kausalya's [his mother's] happiness
like an ocean in profundity - his inmost heart is unfathomable like an ocean

verses.devanagari:
विष्णुना सदृशो वीर्ये सोमवत्प्रियदर्शनः |
कालाग्निसदृशः क्रोधे क्षमया पृथिवीसमः ||
धनदेन समस्त्यागे सत्ये धर्म इवापरः |
verses.iast:
viṣṇunā sadṛśo vīrye somavat priya darśanaḥ |
kāla agni sadṛśaḥ krodhe kṣamayā pṛthvī samaḥ ||
dhanadena samaḥ tyāge satye dharma iva aparaḥ |
verses.translation: "In valour Rama is comparable to Vishnu, and in his looks he is attractive like the moon, he equals the earth in his forgiveness, but he is matchable to world ending fire in his wrath... and in benevolence he is identical to Kubera, God of Wealth, and in his candour he is like Dharma itself, the Truth personified, with none to rival him...
notes: Here the 'valour' is to cause harm to enemy, while remaining himself unharmed... svasya avikāra eva parasya vikāra āpadanam Rama Tilaka. 'Though Rama is Vishnu, but by nature of his incarnation as human, he is different from Vishnu upādhi-bheda... Hence Vishnu has become another entity than Rama... Or, his valour is selfsame to Vishnu's valour because he is selfsame Vishnu...' Govindaraja. 'As there is none other in similitude, he is compared Vishnu, insofar as valour is concerned...' Maheshvara Tiirtha. Earth personally does not grieve when people tread on it, trample, dig, cut, or whatever is done to her. Likewise Rama personally gets unaffected, whatever harm is done to him, but he becomes wrathful, if that harm is committed to dharma.

Readers may find an inordinate use of ellipses in translation of the epic. But they are 'a must.' Pt. Satya Vrat, the author of Ramayana - A Linguistic Study says: "Ellipsis is the peculiarity of the style of the older works like Ramayana... their writings, as they stood, yielded incomplete sense which has to be supplemented by adhyāhāra, viz., supply of words, that would fit in the context... Indeed, in most cases the ellipsis could be readily understood and would suggest the word or words that would make it up...' We therefore request the readers to go by the meaning of the context, than by the order of words, for there is a saying... pāṭhakrame arthakramo balīyaḥ... So, this adhyāhāra, supply of words, may not be that faithful while rendering from Sanskrit to English.

glosses.meaning: attractive in look like the moon
matchable to the world ending fire
equals to the Earth in forgiveness

verses.devanagari:
तमेवं गुणसम्पन्नं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम् ||
ज्येष्ठं श्रेष्ठगुणैर्युक्तं प्रियं दशरथस्सुतम् |
प्रकृतीनां हितैर्युक्तं प्रकृतिप्रियकाम्यया ||
यौवराज्येन संयोक्तुमैच्छत् प्रीत्या महीपतिः |
verses.iast:
tam evam guṇa sampannam rāmam satya parākramam ||
jyeṣṭam śreṣṭa guṇaiḥ yuktam priyam daśarathaḥ sutam |
prakṛtInām hitaiḥ yuktam prakṛti priya kāṃyayā ||
yauva rājyena saṃyoktum aicchat prītyā mahīpatiḥ |
verses.translation: "Lord of the land King Dasaratha with an intent for doing good to the people, affectionately desired to endow with regent-hood to that Rama, the eldest and a dear son to Dasaratha and who possessed such merits with true valour, together with best of qualities, and concerned for welfare of the people....

glosses.meaning: Lord of the land King Dasaratha
doer of works for the welfare of the people
with a desire for doing good to people

verses.devanagari:
तस्याभिषेकसंभारान् दृष्ट्वा भार्याथ कैकयी ||
पुर्वं दत्तवरा देवी वरमेनमयाचत |
विवासनं च रामस्य भरतस्याभिषेचनम् ||
verses.iast:
tasya abhiṣeka sambhārān dṛṣṭvā bhāryā atha kaikayī ||
pūrvam datta varā devī varam enam ayācata |
vivāsanam ca rāmasya bharatasya abhiṣecanam ||
verses.translation: "Then seeing the arrangements for the anointment of Rama as crown-prince, Kaikeyi, the dear wife and a queen of Dasaratha, solicited boons that were once accorded to her by Dasharatha, for the banishment of Rama and anointment of Bharata as boons.

glosses.meaning: having been with previously given boons

verses.devanagari:
स सत्यवचनाद् राजा धर्मपाशेन संयतः |
विवासयामास सुतं रामं दशरथः प्रियम् ||
verses.iast:
sa satya vacanāt rājā dharma pāśena saṃyataḥ |
vivāsayāmāsa sutam rāmam daśarathaḥ priyam ||
verses.translation: "Bound by his true plighted word and by the noose of righteousness that king Dasharatha exiled his dear son Rama to forests.

verses.devanagari:
स जगाम वनं वीरः प्रतिज्ञामनुपालयन् |
पितुर्वचननिर्देशात् कैकेय्याः प्रियकारणात् ||
verses.iast:
sa jagāma vanam vīraḥ pratijñām anupālayan |
pitur vacana nirdeśāt kaikeyyāḥ priya kāraṇāt ||
verses.translation: "That warrior Rama went to forest for pleasing Kaikeyi, and as directed by his father, and to follow his father's word of honour.

glosses.meaning: promise - his own pledge to adhere to his father's word, or, promise of his father to Kaikeyi

verses.devanagari:
तं व्रजन्तं प्रियो भ्राता लक्ष्मणोऽनुजगाम ह |
स्नेहाद्विनयसम्पन्नः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः ||
भ्रातरं दयितो भ्रातुः सौभ्रात्रमनुदर्शयन् |
verses.iast:
taṃ vrajantaṃ priyo bhrātā lakṣmaṇaḥ anujagāma ha |
snehāt vinaya sampannaḥ sumitra ānanda vardhanaḥ ||
bhrātaram dayito bhrātuḥ saubhrātram anu darśayan |
verses.translation: "While that Rama was going on exile, Lakshmana, endowed with humbleness, and augmentor of his mother Sumitra's joy, and a loving and a dear brother to Rama, followed him out of affection, showing brotherly fraternity.
notes: व्रजन्तम् is an accusative case of व्रजत् with व्रज् as its root.

glosses.meaning: while that brother [Rama] was going [to forest].

verses.devanagari:
रामस्य दयिता भार्या नित्यं प्राणसमा हिता ||
जनकस्य कुले जाता देवमायेव निर्मिता |
सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्ना नारीणामुत्तमा वधूः ||
सीताप्यनुगता रामं शशिनं रोहिणी यथा |
verses.iast:
rāmasya dayitā bhāryā nityam prāṇa samā hitā ||
janakasya kule jātā deva māyeva nir.hmitā |
sarva lakṣaṇa sampannā nārīṇām uttamā vadhūḥ ||
sītāpya anugatā rāmam śaśinam rohiṇī yathā |
verses.translation: "Even Seetha, daughter-in-law of Dasaratha, and Rama's beloved wife equalling to Rama's life, ever well disposed, born in the family of Janaka and one as though fashioned by a Divine marvel, endowed with all good characteristics and the best among women, followed Rama to forest, like Rohini following the Moon...
notes: Here devamāyā refers to many concepts. VaiShNavaite tenets tell that the word deva is ascribable only to Vishnu, but not to other gods. Thus, this is ViShNumaayaa, when He assumed an extraordinary female form called Mohini, when distributing amṛta, the divine elixir, to gods and demons. Next is the form of Tilottama, a divine beauty to hoodwink demons called Sunda and Upasunda. The other is Vishnu's līlā śakti, which is divinely fascinating. Yet another is grammatical connotation, mā yā where, mā= Goddess Lakshmi; yā= who that is; meaning yā sītā sā mā= 'who is Goddess Lakshmi... She is Seetha...' and this results in the saying: ati rūpavatī sītā... ati mūrkhaḥ ca rāvaṇa 'While Seetha is extraordinarily beautiful, Ravana is exceedingly stupid...

The deities have their wives always with them. Chandra, the Moon has Rohini, a conspicuous star, while Surya, Sun has Prabha, Sunshine. Minus these wives, their glow and glitter is void. So also, Rama has an inseparable wife. Though Seetha and Lakshmana were not exiled, they followed Rama out of concept of 'togetherness...'

glosses.meaning: born in the family of Janaka
as though fashioned by divine marvel
possessor of all characteristics [befitting to an ideal lady]

verses.devanagari:
पौरैरनुगतो दूरं पित्रा दशरथेन च ||
शृङ्गिबेरपुरे सूतं गङ्गाकूले व्यसर्जयत् |
गुहमासाद्य धर्मात्मा निषादाधिपतिं प्रियम् ||
गुहेन सहितो रामो लक्ष्मणेन च सीतया |
verses.iast:
pauraiḥ anugato dūram pitrā daśarathena ca ||
śṛngibera pure sūtam gaṅgā kūle vyasarjayat |
guham āsādya dharmātmā niṣāda adhipatim priyam ||
guheana sahito rāmo lakśmaṇena ca sītayā |
verses.translation: "The citizens of Ayodhya and his father Dasaratha followed virtuous Rama for a distance when he started on his exile. Later Rama reached the tribal chief named Guha, who liked Rama, on the bank of River Ganga in a town called Sringaberapura. Together with Guha, Lakshmana and Seetha, he left off the charioteer.

glosses.meaning: together with Guha, Lakshmana and Seetha

verses.devanagari:
ते वनेन वनं गत्वा नदीस्तीर्त्वा बहूदकाः ||
चित्रकूटमनुप्राप्य भरद्वाजस्य शासनात् |
रम्यमावसथं कृत्वा रममाणा वने त्रयः ||
देवगन्धर्वसंकाशास्तत्र ते न्यवसन् सुखम् |
verses.iast:
te vanena vanam gatvā nadīḥ tīrtvā bahu udakāḥ ||
citrakūṭam anuprāpya bharadvājasya śāsanāt |
raṃyam āvasatham kṛtvā ramamāṇā vane trayaḥ ||
deva gandharva saṅkāśāḥ tatra te nyavasan sukham |
verses.translation: "That trio of Seetha, Rama and Lakshmana after going from forest to forest and crossing many a river with much waters, by the ordainment of Bharadwaja, arrived at Chitrakuta, and building a handsome cottage there, they lived happily and delightfully in the woods there, like gods and gandharvas...
notes: In another way the meaning is: te avane 'they, protecting each other...' te ramamāṇāḥ ' those two Rama and Seetha, frolicsomely delighted, enjoyed the essence of forest dwelling...' saṅkāśā similar to Vishnu or Narayana's enjoyment of krīḍā rasa 'the essence of His playful acts...' and Lakshmana enjoyed the essence of his servitude sevā rasa and where deva = devī ca devaḥ ca devau 'either goddess or god... it but the Almighty...' gandharva = gānam dhārayati iti gandharva - jīvan muktaḥ attaining liberation while living, thus Lakshmana rejoiced with his singing of sāma gāna of Sama Veda....' And they rejoiced without feeling any difference between city dwelling and forest dwelling... as every part of Universe is theirs.
In another way tevane vanam gatvā 'playfully, to forests, they went...' It is a play for them to enter the forest to resolve the purpose of Ramayana and their incarnations.

verses.devanagari:
चित्रकूटं गते रामे पुत्रशोकातुरस्तदा ||
राजा दशरथः स्वर्गं जगाम विलपन् सुतम् |
verses.iast:
citrakūṭam gate rāme putra śoka āturaḥ tathā ||
rājā daśarathaḥ svargam jagāma vilapan sutam |
verses.translation: "On Rama going to Chitrakuta thus, King Dasharatha tormented by the grief for son, went to heavens weeping for son...
notes: The word 'thus' in the shloka, is according to the text of Govindaraja. Maheshvara Tiirtha's text will have 'then'.

glosses.meaning: tormented by grief for his son

verses.devanagari:
मृते तु तस्मिन् भरतो वसिष्ठप्रमुखैर्द्विजैः ||
नियुज्यमानो राज्याय नैच्छद् राज्यं महाबलः |
स जगाम वनं वीरो रामपादप्रसादकः ||
verses.iast:
mṛte tu tasmin bharato vasiṣṭha pramukhaiḥ dvijaiḥ ||
niyujyamāno rājyāya na icchat rājyam mahābalaḥ |
sa jagāma vanam vīro rāma pāda prasādakaḥ ||
verses.translation: "On Dasharatha's dying, though Bharata had been appointed for kingship by Sage Vashishta and other Brahmanas, that highly mighty one did not desire kingdom. That warrior Bharata went to forest to propitiate the venerable Rama... [1-1-33b. 34]

glosses.meaning: by Sage Vasishta and other prominent Brahmanas

verses.devanagari:
गत्वा तु स महात्मानं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम् |
अयाचद्भ्रातरं राममार्यभावपुरस्कृतः ||
त्वमेव राजा धर्मज्ञ इति रामं वचोऽब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
gatvā tu sa mahātmānam rāmam satya parākramam |
ayācat bhrātaram rāmam ārya bhāva puraskṛtaḥ ||
tvam eva rājā dharmajña iti rāmam vacaḥ abravīt |
verses.translation: "That Bharata, possessed of a worthy way of thinking [to get Rama installed as king], on going to Rama, begged his brother Rama, a great souled one and a truly courageous one. Bharata spoke words in this manner to Rama - "You alone, the knower of probity, be the king." ... '
notes: tu is omitted in the translation since it is there for the purpose of pādapūraṇa.

glosses.meaning: possessed of a worthy way of thinking [to get Rama installed as king]

verses.devanagari:
रामोऽपि परमोदारः सुमुखः सुमहायशाः ||
न चैच्छत्पितुरादेशाद्राज्यं रामो महाबलः |
verses.iast:
rāmo'pi paramodāraḥ sumukhaḥ sumahāyaśāḥ ||
na ca icchat pitur ādeśāt rājyam rāmo mahābalaḥ |
verses.translation: "Even though Rama was very benevolent, gracious also, highly famed and with great prowess, Rama did not desire kingdom due to father's injunction...

verses.devanagari:
पादुके चास्य राज्याय न्यासं दत्त्वा पुनः पुनः ||
निवर्तयामास ततो भरतं भरताग्रजः |
verses.iast:
pāduke ca asya rājyāya nyāsam dattvā punaḥ punaḥ ||
nivartayāmāsa tato bharatam bharata agrajaḥ |
verses.translation: "Thereafter, repeatedly turning Bharata back, the elder brother, Rama, gave his wooden shoes to Bharata and entrusting them to represent him for the sake of kingdom.

verses.devanagari:
स काममनवाप्यैव रामपादावुपस्पृशन् ||
नन्दिग्रामेऽकरोद्राज्यं रामागमनकाङ्क्षया |
verses.iast:
sa kāmam anavāpya eva rāma pādā upaspṛśan ||
nandi grāme akarot rājyam rāma āgamana kāṅkṣayā |
verses.translation: "That Bharata, thus with a desire unfulfilled, ruled the kingdom from Nandigrama, touching Rama's sandals representing feet of Rama, with an expectation of Rama's arrival...

glosses.meaning: from Nandigrama [a village,] carried on, kingdom

verses.devanagari:
गते तु भरते श्रीमान् सत्यसन्धो जितेन्द्रियः ||
रामस्तु पुनरालक्ष्य नागरस्य जनस्य च |
तत्रागमनमेकाग्रो दण्डकान्प्रविवेश ह |
verses.iast:
gate tu bharate śrīmān satyasandho jitendriyaḥ ||
rāmaḥ tu punaḥ ālakṣya nāgarasya janasya ca |
tatra āgamanam ekāgro daṇḍakān praviveśa ha |
verses.translation: "On the departure of Bharata, that splendid Rama, truth-bound, and self-controlled, anticipated the repeated visits of citizens and other people. To be undisturbed, Rama then entered Dandaka forests...
notes: The translation of ekāgraḥ as "undisturbed" is done according to the context of Rama's anticipation that there might be repeated visits from various people to Chitrakuta and entreaties from them for Rama to return to Ayodhya. Normally ekāgraḥ is translated as "single-pointed attention". Govindaraja explains ekāgraḥ with respect to following father's injunction or being alert to increased presence of RakShasaas.

verses.devanagari:
प्रविश्य तु महारण्यं रामो राजीवलोचनः |
विराधं राक्षसं हत्वा शरभङ्गं ददर्श ह ||
सुतीक्ष्णं चाप्यगस्त्यं च अगस्त्यभ्रातरं तथा |
verses.iast:
praviśya tu mahāaraṇyam rāmo rājīva locanaḥ |
virādham rākṣasam hatvā śarabhaṅgam dadarśa ha ||
sutīkṣṇam ca api agastyam ca agastya bhrātaram tathā |
verses.translation: "That lotus-eyed Rama, on his entering the vast Dandaka forest, killed the demon Viraadha, and indeed beheld Sage Sharabhanga and also Sage Suteekhsna, Sage Agastya and likewise Sage Agastya's brother...
notes: The name of Agastya's brother is Sudarshana, and he will never be called by his own name, but will be called as agatsyabhrātā, brother of Agastya.
tu is omitted in the translation since it is there for the purpose of pādapūraṇa.

glosses.meaning: and on killing the demon Viradha
indeed beheldsharabhaN^gam sutiikshNam ca api = Sage Sharabhanga and also Sage Suteekshna

verses.devanagari:
अगस्त्यवचनाच्चैव जग्राहैन्द्रं शरासनम् ||
खड्गं च परमप्रीतस्तूणी चाक्षयसायकौ |
verses.iast:
agastya vacanāt ca eva jagrāha aindram śarāsanam ||
khaḍgam ca parama prītaḥ tūṇī ca akṣaya sāyakau |
verses.translation: "On Sage Agastya's word, Rama, with great delight, received from Agastya, Indra's bow along with the sword and two quivers with ever replenishing arrows...

glosses.meaning: And according to Sage Agastya's word alone

verses.devanagari:
वसतस्तस्य रामस्य वने वनचरैः सह ||
ऋषयोऽभ्यागमन्सर्वे वधायासुररक्षसाम् |
verses.iast:
vasataḥ tasya rāmasya vane vana caraiḥ saha ||
ṛṣayaḥ abhyāgaman sarve vadhāya asura rakṣasām |
verses.translation: "During Rama's stay in the forest, all the sages together with other forest dwellers, approached him for the elimination of ogres and demons...

glosses.meaning: for the killing of ogres and demons

verses.devanagari:
स तेषां प्रतिशुश्राव राक्षसानां तथा वने ||
प्रतिज्ञातश्च रामेण वधः संयति रक्षसाम् |
ऋषीणामग्निकल्पानां दण्डकारण्यवासिनाम् ||
verses.iast:
sa teṣAm prati śuśrāva rāxasānām tathā vane ||
pratijñātaḥ ca rāmeṇa vadhaḥ saṃyati rakśasām |
ṛṣīṇām agni kalpānām daṇḍakāraṇya vāsīnām ||
verses.translation: "He [Rama] agreed to that supplication of those sages dwelling in the forest of demons. A promise was also made by Rama to the sages who equalled the fire and who were living in that Dandaka forest about killing of the demons in combat...
notes: The word asura is as from asūn rāti iti asura: asu = life; ra= taker; i.e., life takers - demons, while the word sura is nectar consuming one, the divine. In later chapters of this canto, accounts are given as how these were created and named.

verses.devanagari:
तेन तत्रैव वसता जनस्थाननिवासिनी |
विरूपिता शूर्पणखा राक्षसी कामरूपिणी ||
verses.iast:
tena tatra eva vasatā janasthāna nivāsinī |
virūpitā śūrpaṇakhā rākṣasī kāma rūpiṇī ||
verses.translation: "While Rama was living there in the Dandaka forest, a guise-changing demoness named Shuurpa-nakha, who was a resident of Janasthana, a portion of Dandaka forest, was disfigured by him...
notes: Readers are referred to the verse 3-18-20 where Rama asks Lakshmana to deface Shuurpa-nakha who carries out the act of cutting the nose and ears of this demoness, which is the turning point of the story. From this verse it is clear that Rama is instrumental in the disfiguring of Shuurpa-nakha.

Shuurpa-nakha is so named because her fingernails are like winnowing fans, śūrpatulyanakhā iti śūrpanakhā; śūrpa= winnowing fan; tulya = like; nakhā = fingernails. She is the sister of Ravana the main antogonist of the epic, and she is the actual trouble creator in the epic.

glosses.meaning: a resident of Janasthana [a portion of Dandaka forest]

verses.devanagari:
ततः शूर्पणखावाक्यादुद्युक्तान् सर्वराक्षसान् |
खरं त्रिशिरसं चैव दूषणं चैव राक्षसम् ||
निजघान रणे रामस्तेषां चैव पदानुगान् |
verses.iast:
tataḥ śUrpaṇakhā vākyāt udyuktān sarva rākṣasān |
kharam triśirasam ca eva dūṣaṇam ca eva rākṣasam ||
nijaghāna raṇe rāmaḥ teṣām ca eva pada anugān |
verses.translation: "Then in a battle, Rama killed all demons who became zealously active incited by Suurphanakha's words, including the demons Khara, Trishira, Duushana together with all of their foot-followers...
notes: We are ignoring in translation the एव part of चैव and translating the word चैव as "and".

glosses.meaning: Then Rama in a battle killed

verses.devanagari:
वने तस्मिन्निवसता जनस्थाननिवासिनाम् ||
रक्षसां निहतान्यासन् सहस्राणि चतुर्दश |
verses.iast:
vane tasmin nivasatā janasthāna nivāsinām ||
rakṣasām nihatāni asan sahasrāṇi catur daśa |
verses.translation: "During Rama's stay in that forest, fourteen thousand demon inhabitants of Janasthana became slain...

glosses.meaning: During his stay in that forest

verses.devanagari:
ततो ज्ञातिवधं श्रुत्वा रावणः क्रोधमूर्छितः ||
सहायं वरयामास मारीचं नाम राक्षसम् |
verses.iast:
tato jñāti vadham śrutvā rāvaṇaḥ krodha mūrchitaḥ ||
sahāyam varayāmāsa mārīcam nāma rākṣasam |
verses.translation: "Then, on hearing the slaughter of his kinsmen, Ravana convulsed in anger and sought to get the help of a demon named Maareecha...
notes: Ravana is the supremo of demons and the main antagonist in this epic. His name is Dashagriiva, meaning that he has ten heads. This name 'Ravana' obtains from the root ru - śabde rāvayati iti rāvaṇaḥ 'one who makes people cry by his violent actions...' and it also means viśravasaḥ apatyam pumān rāvaṇaḥ, viśravaso viśravaṇa-ravaṇau 'the son of one named Vishravasa...' Govindaraja.
वरयामास is the लिट् लकार of of the root वर (see आत्मनेपदी form)

glosses.meaning: on hearing the slaughter of [his] kinsmen

verses.devanagari:
वार्यमाणः सुबहुशो मारीचेन स रावणः ||
न विरोधो बलवता क्षमो रावण तेन ते |
verses.iast:
vāryamāṇaḥ subahuśo mārīcena sa rāvaṇaḥ ||
na virodho balavatā kṣamo rāvaṇa tena te |
verses.translation: "But Maareecha restrained Ravana telling him many times, 'Oh, Ravana! Rivarly with that formidable Rama is not appropriate of you...'

verses.devanagari:
अनादृत्य तु तद्वाक्यं रावणः कालचोदितः ||
जगाम सहमारीचस्तस्याश्रमपदं तदा |
verses.iast:
anādṛtya tu tat vākyam rāvaṇaḥ kāla coditaḥ ||
jagāma saha mārīcaḥ tasya āśrama padam tadā |
verses.translation: "Then disregarding Maareecha's words and impelled by his own fate, Ravana advanced to the place of Rama's hermitage along with Maareecha...

verses.devanagari:
तेन मायाविना दूरमपवाह्य नृपात्मजौ ||
जहार भार्यां रामस्य गृध्रं हत्वा जटायुषम् |
verses.iast:
tena māyāvinā dūram apavāhya nṛpa ātmajau ||
jahāra bhāryām rāmasya gṛdhram hatvā jaṭāyuṣam |
verses.translation: "After taking away of Rama and Lakshmana to a distance by the trickster Maareecha, Ravana stole Rama's wife after killing Jatayu...

glosses.meaning: [Ravana] stole Rama's, wifejaTaayuSam gR^idhram hatvaa = after killing Jatayu

verses.devanagari:
गृध्रं च निहतं दृष्ट्वा हृतां श्रुत्वा च मैथिलीम् ||
राघवः शोकसन्तप्तो विललापाकुलेन्द्रियः |
verses.iast:
gṛdhram ca nihatam dṛṣṭvā hṛtām śrutvā ca maithilīm ||
rāghavaḥ śoka santapto vilalāpa ākula indriyaḥ |
verses.translation: "Raghava on seeing the smitten Jatayu and also on hearing about Seetha's abduction, wailed with disturbed senses, seething with anguish ...

glosses.meaning: on seeing the smitten vulture Jatayu
and also on hearing about Mythili's [Seetha's] abduction

verses.devanagari:
ततस्तेनैव शोकेन गृध्रं दग्ध्वा जटायुषम् ||
मार्गमाणो वने सीतां राक्षसं संददर्श ह |
कबन्धं नाम रूपेण विकृतं घोरदर्शनम् ||
verses.iast:
tataḥ tena eva śokena gṛdhram dag.hdhvā jaṭāyuṣam ||
mārgamāṇo vane sītām rākṣasam sandadarśa ha |
kabandham nāma rūpeṇa vikṛtam ghora da.rśanam ||
verses.translation: "Rama then cremated that vulture Jataayu with that state of anguish, and while searching for Seetha in forest, he indeed saw a demon named Kabandha, deformed in his looks and with a terrible appearance...

glosses.meaning: while searching [for] Seetha in that forest

verses.devanagari:
तं निहत्य महाबाहुर्ददाह स्वर्गतश्च सः |
स चास्य कथयामास शबरीं धर्मचारिणीम् ||
श्रमणीं धर्मनिपुणामभिगच्छेति राघव |
verses.iast:
tam nihatya mahābāhuḥ dadāha svargataḥ ca saḥ |
sa ca asya kathayāmāsa śabarīm dharma cāriṇīm ||
śramaṇām dharma nipuṇām abhigaccha iti rāghava |
verses.translation: "That Rama with great arms after slaying Kabandha, cremated him and Kabandha obtanined heaven. Before going to heaven, he spoke thus to Rama: 'Oh Raghava! You proceed to Sabari, a lady with righteous conduct, an expert in probity and a devotee.'...

glosses.meaning: she who is an expert in probity

verses.devanagari:
सोऽभ्यगच्छन्महातेजाः शबरीं शत्रुसूदनः ||
शबर्या पूजितः सम्यग्रामो दशरथात्मजः |
verses.iast:
saḥ abhya gacchan mahātejāḥ śabarīm śatru sūdanaḥ ||
śaba.ryā pūjitaḥ saṃyak rāmo daśaratha ātmajaḥ |
verses.translation: "That great resplendent Rama, the son of Dasaratha, an anhillator of enemies, approached Sabari and was thoroughly honoured by her...
notes: Next verse onwards the episodes in KiShkindha are introduced. Now Rama meets Hanuma, the Vaanara. vanena= in forests, carati= moves about, iti= thus; therefore vānara = 'forest-ranger' is the declination of the term Vaanara. Traditionally Hanuma is worshipped as a god.

verses.devanagari:
पम्पातीरे हनुमता सङ्गतो वानरेण ह ||
हनुमद्वचनाच्चैव सुग्रीवेण समागतः |
verses.iast:
pampā tīre hanumatā saṅgato vānareṇa ha ||
hanumat vacanāt ca eva sugrīveṇa samāgataḥ |
verses.translation: "Rama was united indeed with the Vanara Hanuma on the banks of Lake Pampa, and upon the word of Hanuma, Rama met with Sugreeva...

glosses.meaning: [Rama was] indeed united with the Vanara Hanuma

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीवाय च तत्सर्वं शंसद्रामो महाबलः ||
आदितस्तद्यथावृत्तं सीतायाश्च विशेषतः |
verses.iast:
sugrīvāya ca tat sarvam śaṃsat rāmo mahābalaḥ ||
āditaḥ tat yathā vṛttam sītāyāḥ ca viśeṣataḥ |
verses.translation: "The highly powerful Rama detailed from the beginning all that happened, and in particular the abduction of Seetha, to Sugriva and to Hanuma also...
notes: Here the use of 'highly powerful...' for Rama is to indicate that though he himself was capable enough to eliminate Ravana, but as a human, he needed some agency, since humans in such difficulties are usually in need of a helping hand. As such, Rama had to befriend Sugreeva and it was necessary to narrate all sad episodes to his friend.

glosses.meaning: and in particular [the abduction] of Seetha

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीवश्चापि तत्सर्वं श्रुत्वा रामस्य वानरः ||
चकार सख्यं रामेण प्रीतश्चैवाग्निसाक्षिकम् |
verses.iast:
sugrīvaḥ ca api tat sarvam śrutvā rāmasya vānaraḥ ||
cakāra sakhyam rāmeṇa prītaḥ ca eva agni sākśikam |
verses.translation: "The Vanara Sugreeva after listening to all that talk of Rama made friendship with Rama delightedly with sacred fire as witness...

glosses.meaning: with fire [flaring auspicious fire] as witness also thus.

verses.devanagari:
ततो वानरराजेन वैरानुकथनं प्रति ||
रामायावेदितं सर्वं प्रणयाद्दुःखितेन च |
verses.iast:
tato vānara rājena vaira anukathanam prati ||
rāmāya āveditam sarvam praṇayāt duḥkhitena ca |
verses.translation: "Then out of affection, the incident was related with regard to Sugreeva's enemity with Vali in its entirety by the Vanara King with grief to Rama ...

glosses.meaning: by the Vanara King with grief

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिज्ञातं च रामेण तदा वालिवधं प्रति ||
वालिनश्च बलं तत्र कथयामास वानरः |
verses.iast:
pratijñātam ca rāmeṇa tadā vāli vadham prati ||
vālinaḥ ca balam tatra kathayāmāsa vānaraḥ |
verses.translation: "Then a solemn promise was made by Rama with regards to killing of Vali. In that regard Vanara Sugreeva also described Vali's strength...
notes: Vali, the elder brother of Sugreeva, is another principle character of Ramayana. He is capable of rendering oblations to gods in the wee hours of a single day in four oceans on four sides of the globe, by his flying from one ocean to the other. He is mightier than Ravana, the chief villain of the epic, and Ravana was subdued by Vali's strength. As a preamble to the incident of eliminating mighty Ravana in the last book of the epic, this episode of eliminating a still mightier monkey is the stepping-stone for the climactic victory.

glosses.meaning: with regards to killing of Vali

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीवः शङ्कितश्चासीन्नित्यं वीर्येण राघवे ||
राघवप्रत्ययार्थं तु दुन्दुभेः कायमुत्तमम् |
दर्शयामास सुग्रीवो महापर्वतसन्निभम् ||
verses.iast:
sugrīvaḥ śaṅkitaḥ ca āsīt nityam vīryeṇa rāghave ||
rāghavaḥ pratyayārtham tu dundubheḥ kāyam uttamam |
darśayāmāsa sugrīvaḥ mahāparvata saṃnibham ||
verses.translation: "But Sugreeva remained ever doubtful with respect to Raghava, about Raghava's prowess. Sugreeva showed Dundubhi's big and great mountain-like dead body to gain confidence in Raghava...
notes: Vali had at one time killed Dundubhi and kicked his body over a long distance.

verses.devanagari:
उत्स्मयित्वा महाबाहुः प्रेक्ष्य चास्थि महाबलः |
पादाङ्गुष्ठेन चिक्षेप सम्पूर्णं दशयोजनम् ||
verses.iast:
utsmayitvā mahābāhuḥ prekśya ca asti mahābalaḥ |
pāda aṅguṣṭena cikśepa sampūrṇam daśa yojanam ||
verses.translation: Great armed and very powerful Rama after seeing the bones of Dundubhi smiled and by the big toe of his foot threw it wholly for ten yojana-s length.
notes: Vali was able to throw that body, with whole of his foot, only up to two hundred bow-lengths, where the length of bow is said as six to seven feet. But Rama could kick that heap to ten yojana lengths, roughly ninety miles, only with a flip of his foot-toe's tip. But Sugreeva continued his grumbling, 'in those days this skeleton was with flesh and blood, now it became weight-less, thus show me more of your show of strength...' One Yojana is an ancient measure for distance, where that distance is covered in one yoking. Chambers dictionary puts it as five miles, and it is not agreeable for it was British-Indian revenue measure. Traditionally it is four krosha-s and thus each yojana is nine to ten miles.

Govindaraja cleaves the compound utsmayitvā to ut smayitvā and takes ut 'to up...' and fixes it to cikṣepa to mean ut cikṣepa 'up-heaved and hurled...' and smayitva comes to mean 'smiling self-assuredly, or smiling self-composedly...' And Maheshvara Tiirtha says that 'when all-wise-knowers are not able to know what I am, there is no surprise if a monkey in a remote forest doubts my capability... let him see a speck of it...' thus Rama smiled in aplomb...'

And the often repeated epithet to Rama mahābāhuḥ means not just 'yards and yards of lengthy arms...dangling up to knees..' but 'one who does unimaginable deeds...' and his arms are the unusual instruments to perform such unusual tasks, hence ambidextrous, or omni-dextrous...

glosses.meaning: and by the big toe of his foot

verses.devanagari:
बिभेद च पुनः सालान् सप्तैकेन महेषुणा |
गिरिं रसातलं चैव जनयन् प्रत्ययं तदा ||
verses.iast:
bibheda ca punaḥ sālān sapta ekena mahā iṣuṇā |
girim rasātalam caiva janayan pratyayam tathā ||
verses.translation: "Then again Rama ripped through seven massive Sala trees with only one great arrow, which not only went through the trees but also rent through a mountain, and to the nethermost subterranean of earth, in order to create faith in the mind of Sugreeva...
notes: The rasātala is deepest subterranean plane, and it forms the base of other planes of earth called, atala, vitala, sutala, talātala, mahātala, rasātala underneath the surface of earth up to its core.

glosses.meaning: to create faith [in the mind of Sugreeva]

verses.devanagari:
ततः प्रीतमनाश्चैव विश्वस्तश्च महाकपिः |
किष्किन्धां रामसहितो जगाम च गुहां तदा ||
verses.iast:
tataḥ prīta manāḥ tena viśvastaḥ sa mahākapiḥ |
kiṣkindhām rāma sahito jagāma ca guhām tadā ||
verses.translation: "Thereafter great monkey Sugreeva with a gladdened heart by that act of Rama, proceeded to cave-like Kishkindha then along with Rama and with confidence in Rama's strength...

verses.devanagari:
ततोऽगर्जद्धरिवरः सुग्रीवो हेमपिङ्गलः |
तेन नादेन महता निर्जगाम हरीश्वरः ||
verses.iast:
tataḥ agarjat harivaraḥ sugrīvo hema piṅgalaḥ |
tena nādena mahatā nirjagāma harīśvaraḥ ||
verses.translation: "Then that best monkey Sugreeva, with a golden hue, made a roaring sound. By that loud sound, the king of monkeys, Vali, emerged out...

verses.devanagari:
अनुमान्य तदा तारां सुग्रीवेण समागतः |
निजघान च तत्रैनं शरेणैकेन राघवः ||
verses.iast:
anumānya tadā tārām sugrīveṇa samāgataḥ |
nijaghāna ca tatra enam śareṇa ekena rāghavaḥ ||
verses.translation: "Then after Tara [wife of Vali] permitting, Vali met with Sugreeva in a combat. And Rama killed this Vali with a single arrow there...

verses.devanagari:
ततः सुग्रीववचनाद्धत्वा वालिनमाहवे |
सुग्रीवमेव तद्राज्ये राघवः प्रत्यपादयत् ||
verses.iast:
tataḥ sugrīva vacanāt hatvā vālinam āhave |
sugrīvam eva tat rājye rāghavaḥ pratyapādayat ||
verses.translation: "Then Raghava after killing Vali in a combat as per Sugreeva's plea, installed Sugreeva alone as the king of Vanaras..

glosses.meaning: after killing Vali in a combat

verses.devanagari:
स च सर्वान् समानीय वानरान् वानरर्षभः |
दिशः प्रस्थापयामास दिदृक्षुर्जनकात्मजाम् ||
verses.iast:
sa ca sarvān samānīya vānarān vānararṣabhaḥ |
diśaḥ prasthāpayāmāsa didṛkṣuḥ janaka ātmajām ||
verses.translation: "That best among monkeys, Sugreeva, after summoning all Vanaras, dispatched them in different directions to behold the daughter of Janaka...
notes: Sugreeva was acclaimed to be a strict disciplinarian, and his orders were inviolable by anyone. Even now the proverbial saying exists that a "command by elders is to be followed like sugreevājñā 'Sugreeva's order'.

verses.devanagari:
ततो गृध्रस्य वचनात्सम्पातेेर्हनुमान् बली |
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं पुप्लुवे लवणार्णवम् ||
verses.iast:
tato gṛdhrasya vacanāt sampāteḥ hanumān balī |
śata yojana vistīrṇam pupluve lavaṇa arṇavam ||
verses.translation: "After that, the strong Hanuma, upon the word of the vulture Sampati who was elder brother of Jatayu, flew across the salty ocean one hundred yojanas in breadth...

glosses.meaning: upon the word of the vulture Sampati

verses.devanagari:
तत्र लङ्कां समासाद्य पुरीं रावणपालिताम् |
ददर्श सीतां ध्यायन्तीमशोकवनिकां गताम् ||
verses.iast:
tatra laṅkām samāsādya purīm rāvaṇa pālitām |
dadarśa sītām dhyāyantīm aśoka vanikām gatām ||
verses.translation: "On reaching the city of Lanka ruled by Ravana, Hanuma saw Seetha situated in Ashoka gardens there and meditating on Rama alone...

verses.devanagari:
निवेदयित्वाभिज्ञानं प्रवृत्तिं च निवेद्य च |
समाश्वास्य च वैदेहीं मर्दयामास तोरणम् ||
verses.iast:
nivedayitvā abhijñānam pravṛttim ca nivedya ca |
samāśvāsya ca vaidehīm mardayāmāsa toraṇam ||
verses.translation: "After delivering to Seetha the mark of identification in the form of a ring from Rama and also communicating Rama's disposition and consoling Vaidehi, Hanuma destroyed the welcome-arch of Ashoka gardens...

verses.devanagari:
पञ्च सेनाग्रगान् हत्वा सप्त मन्त्रिसुतानपि |
शूरमक्षं च निष्पिष्य ग्रहणं समुपागमत् ||
verses.iast:
pañca sena agragān hatvā sapta mantri sutān api |
śūram akṣam ca niṣpiṣya grahaṇam samupāgamat ||
verses.translation: "After killing five army chiefs and seven minister's sons and crushing the valiant Aksha, Hanuma got into state of captivity...

glosses.meaning: Hanuma got into state of captivity.

verses.devanagari:
अस्त्रेणोन्मुक्तमात्मानं ज्ञात्वा पैतामहाद्वरात् |
मर्षयन् राक्षसान् वीरो यन्त्रिणस्तान्यदृच्छया ||
ततो दग्ध्वा पुरीं लङ्कामृते सीतां च मैथिलीम् |
रामाय प्रियमाख्यातुं पुनरायान्महाकपिः ||
verses.iast:
astreṇa unmuktam ātmānam jñātvā paitāmahāt varāt |
marṣayan rākṣasān vīro yantriṇaḥ tān yadṛcchayā ||
tato dagdhvā purīm laṅkām ṛte sītām ca maithilīm |
rāmāya priyam ākhyātum punaḥ āyāt mahākapiḥ ||
verses.translation: "Knowing himself to be free from the captivity of the weapon according to Brahma's boon, the valiant great monkey Hanuma enduring those demons with self-will who tied his tail with ropes with the intention of burning it, there after burning the city of Lanka while leaving from fire the Seetha of Mithila, got back again to convey the pleasant news to Rama ...
notes: This is in sundara kaanDa. Hanuma sees Ravana and others in the court, and as a show of his strength burns down Lanka except the place where Seetha is stationed, only to prove that the riches and wealth enjoyed at the cost others will burn down to ashes some day, besides Vibheeshana's place, for Vibheeshana is the adherer of Dharma. This episode is to relegate the false pride of Ravana, and as a symbolic suggestion that pomp and effluence without virtue are short lived.

glosses.meaning: to be free from the [captivity of] weapon
who tied [ his tail with ropes]
to convey the pleasant [news] to Rama.

verses.devanagari:
सोऽभिगम्य महात्मानं कृत्वा रामं प्रदक्षिणम् |
न्यवेदयदमेयात्मा दृष्टा सीतेति तत्त्वतः ||
verses.iast:
saḥ abhigaṃya mahātmānam kṛtvā rāmam pradakṣiṇam |
nyavedayat ameyātmā dṛṣṭā sītā iti tattvataḥ ||
verses.translation: "Approaching the great Rama and peforming circumambulation around Rama, Hanuma having an inestimable intelligence, submitted in essence thus: 'Seen Seetha...'

verses.devanagari:
ततः सुग्रीवसहितो गत्वा तीरं महोदधेः |
समुद्रं क्षोभयामास शरैरादित्यसन्निभैः ||
verses.iast:
tataḥ sugrīva sahito gatvā tīram mahā udadheḥ |
samudram kṣobhayāmāsa śaraiḥ āditya sannibhaiḥ ||
verses.translation: "There-after, Rama along with Sugreeva and other monkeys went to the shore of Great Ocean, and put the Ocean-god to turmoil with his arrows comparable to the Sun...
notes: Rama became angry at the ocean for not yielding way to Lanka. In order to make way through the Ocean, Rama starts depleting its waters with arrows.

glosses.meaning: On going to the Ocean's shore
with arrows comparable to the Sun.

verses.devanagari:
दर्शयामास चात्मानं समुद्रः सरितां पतिः |
समुद्रवचनाच्चैव नलं सेतुमकारयत् ||
verses.iast:
darśayāmāsa ca ātmānam samudraḥ saritām patiḥ |
samudra vacanāt ca eva nalam setum akārayat ||
verses.translation: "The Ocean-god revealed himself and upon his word, Nala built the bridge across the ocean...
notes: Nala, a Vanara engineer, had a boon from his mother. In his childhood he used to throw playthings into water wanting them to float. But they were all submerged. His mother then gave a boon to him saying that whatever article he throws in waters will float, may they be toys or stones or boulders. Here that boon is taken advantage of, and a boulder bridge is built on ocean waters.

glosses.meaning: Ocean-god the lord of the rivers
and upon the words of the Ocean-God
Nala built the bridge [across the ocean].

verses.devanagari:
तेन गत्वा पुरीं लङ्कां हत्वा रावणमाहवे |
रामः सीतामनुप्राप्य परां व्रीडामुपागमत् ||
verses.iast:
tena gatvā purīm laṅkām hatvā rāvaṇam āhave |
rāmaḥ sītām anuprāpya parām vrīḍām upāgamat ||
verses.translation: "Rama, having gone to the city of Lanka by that bridge, killing Ravana in a battle, experienced great shame on getting Seetha back...

glosses.meaning: having gone to the city of Lanka

verses.devanagari:
तामुवाच ततो रामः परुषं जनसंसदि |
अमृष्यमाणा सा सीता विवेश ज्वलनं सती ||
verses.iast:
tām uvāca tataḥ rāmaḥ paruṣam jana saṃsadi |
amṛṣyamāṇā sā sītā viveśa jvalanam satī ||
verses.translation: "There-after, Rama spoke harshly to Seetha in the assembly of the people. Being devoted to her husband, that Seetha, intolerant of the harsh words of Rama, entered into burning fire...

glosses.meaning: in the assembly of the people
intolerant [of the harsh words of Rama]

verses.devanagari:
ततोऽग्निवचनात्सीतां ज्ञात्वा विगतकल्मषाम् |
कर्मणा तेन महता त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ||
सदेवर्षिगणं तुष्टं राघवस्य महात्मनः ||
बभौ रामः संप्रहृष्टः पूजितः सर्वदैवतैः||
verses.iast:
tataḥ agni vacanāt sītām jñātvā vigata kalmaṣām |
karmaṇā tena mahatā trailokyam sa carācaram ||
sa devarṣi gaṇam tuṣṭam rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ ||
babhau rāmaḥ samprahṛṣṭaḥ pūjitaḥ sarva devataiḥ ||
verses.translation: "Then, upon the word of Fire-god, having known Seetha to be sinless, Rama became extremely glad. Worshipped by all gods he became resplendent. By that accomplishment of the great Raghava the three worlds together with mobile and immobile beings, and with groups of gods and sages became exultant...

glosses.meaning: Then upon the word of the Fire-god
by that great accomplishment - of eliminating Ravana
with groups of gods and sages

verses.devanagari:
अभिषिच्य च लङ्कायां राक्षसेन्द्रं विभीषणम् |
कृतकृत्यस्ततो रामो विज्वरः प्रमुमोद ह ||
verses.iast:
abhyaṣicya ca laṅkāyām rākṣasa indram vibhīṣaṇam |
kṛtakṛtyaḥ tadā rāmo vijvaraḥ pramumoda ha ||
verses.translation: "Enthroning Vibheeshana as the chieftain of demons in Lanka, and with a done deed, Rama then rejoiced highly indeed free from distress...

verses.devanagari:
देवताभ्यो वरं प्राप्य समुत्थाप्य च वानरान् |
अयोध्यां प्रस्थितो रामः पुष्पकेण सुहृद् वृतः ||
verses.iast:
devatābhyo varām prāpya samutthāpya ca vānarān |
ayodhyām prasthitaḥ rāmaḥ puṣpakeṇa suhṛt vṛtaḥ ||
verses.translation: "After obtaining a boon from the gods, Rama raised up monkeys from death. He then travelled to Ayodhya by Pushpaka aircraft surrounded by good hearted ones...

glosses.meaning: after obtaining a boon from the gods

verses.devanagari:
भरद्वाजाश्रमं गत्वा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः |
भरतस्यान्तिकं रामो हनुमन्तं व्यसर्जयत् ||
verses.iast:
bharadvāja āśramam gatvā rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ |
bharatasya antikam rāmo hanūmantam vyasarjayat ||
verses.translation: "Rama, with true valour, on going to sage Bharadwaja's hermitage, sent Hanuma to the presence of Bharata...

glosses.meaning: on going to Sage Bharadwaja's hermitage

verses.devanagari:
पुनराख्यायिकां जल्पन् सुग्रीवसहितश्च सः |
पुष्पकं तत्समारुह्य नन्दिग्रामं ययौ तदा ||
verses.iast:
punaḥ ākhyāyikām jalpan sugrīva sahitaḥ tadā |
puṣpakam tat samārūhya nandigrāmam yayau tadā ||
verses.translation: "Then, having boarded Pushpaka aircraft again after leaving the hermitage of Bharadwaja, and narrating past history to Sugreeva and others about the events in the days of his exile in forests, while flying overhead of the very same places, Rama went to Nandigrama...

verses.devanagari:
नन्दिग्रामे जटां हित्वा भ्रातृभिः सहितोऽनघः |
रामः सीतामनुप्राप्य राज्यं पुनरवाप्तवान् ||
verses.iast:
nandigrāme jaṭām hitvā bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito anaghaḥ |
rāmaḥ sītām anuprāpya rājyam punaḥ avāptavān ||
verses.translation: "That sinless Rama rejoining with all of his brothers in the village Nandigrama removed his matted hair. Thus he, on regaining Seetha and on discarding hermit's role again became a householder, and he regained his kingdom also...

verses.devanagari:
प्रहृष्टमुदितो लोकस्तुष्टः पुष्टः सुधार्मिकः |
निरामयो ह्यरोगश्च दुर्भिक्षभयवर्जितः ||
verses.iast:
prahṛṣṭo mudito lokaḥ tuṣṭaḥ puṣṭaḥ sudhārmikaḥ |
nirāmayo hi arogaḥ ca dur.hbhikṣa bhaya varjitaḥ ||
verses.translation: "When Rama is ruling the world will be highly rejoiced and happy, satisfied and abundant, also very righteous, wholesome, disease-free, and free from fear of famine..." Thus Narada is foreseeing the future and telling Valmiki.

verses.devanagari:
न पुत्रमरणं किंचिद्द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुरुषाः क्वचित् |
नार्यश्चाविधवा नित्यं भविष्यन्ति पतिव्रताः ||
verses.iast:
na putra maraṇam kecit drakṣyanti puruṣāḥ kvacit |
nāryaḥ ca avidhavā nityam bhaviṣyanti pati vratāḥ ||
verses.translation: "While Rama is on the throne men will not see the deaths of their children anywhere in their lifetime, and the ladies will remain husband-devouted and unwidowed during their lifetime...

verses.devanagari:
न चाग्निजं भयं किञ्चिन्नाप्सु मज्जन्ति जन्तवः |
न वातजं भयं किञ्चिन्नापि ज्वरकृतं तथा ||
न चापि क्षुद्भयं तत्र न तस्करभयं तथा |
verses.iast:
na ca agnijam bhayam kincit na apsu majjanti jantavaḥ |
na vātajam bhayam kincit na api jvara kṛtam tathā ||
na ca api kśut bhayam tatra na taskara bhayam tathā |
verses.translation: "In the kingdom of Rama, there will be no fear for his subjects from wildfires, gale-storms or from diseases, and there will be no fear from hunger or thieves, nor the cattle will be drowned in floodwaters as well...

glosses.meaning: cattle will not drown in water
not even fear caused by hunger

verses.devanagari:
नगराणि च राष्ट्राणि धनधान्ययुतानि च ||
नित्यं प्रमुदिताः सर्वे यथा कृतयुगे तथा |
verses.iast:
nagarāṇi ca rāṣṭrāṇi dhana dhānya yutāni ca ||
nityam pramuditāḥ sarve yathā kṛta yuge tathā |
verses.translation: "Cities and states as well will be replete with wealth and grains likewise. All his subjects will be highly glad always, like in Krita yuga...

glosses.meaning: [will be replete with] wealth and grains
[all his subjects will be] highly glad always sarve kR^itayuge yathaa = like in Krita yuga .

verses.devanagari:
अश्वमेधशतैरिष्ट्वा तथा बहुसुवर्णकैः ||
गवां कोट्ययुतं दत्त्वा विद्वद्भ्यो विधिपूर्वकम् | |
असंख्येयं धनं दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणेभ्यो महायशाः ||
verses.iast:
aśvamedha śataiḥ iṣṭvā tathā bahu suva.rṇakaiḥ ||
gavām koṭyayutam dattvā vidvabhyo vidhi pūrvakam |
asaṅkhyeyam dhanam dattvā brāhmaṇebho mahāyaśāḥ ||
verses.translation: "Like-wise the highly illustrious Rama having performed hundreds of horse rituals and having donated plentiful gold and crores of cows and wealth that cannot be counted to Brahmanas and to scholars according to custom...

verses.devanagari:
राजवंशान् शतगुणान् स्थापयिष्यति राघवः |
चातुर्वर्ण्यं च लोकेऽस्मिन् स्वे स्वे धर्मे नियोक्ष्यति ||
verses.iast:
rāja vaṃśān śata guṇān sthāpa iṣyati rāghavaḥ |
cātur varṇyam ca loke asmin sve sve dharme niyokṣyati ||
verses.translation: "In this world Raghava will establish kingly dynasties in hundredfold and he will be maintaining the four-caste system positing each in his own duty, may it be caste-bound or provincial-kingdom-bound duty, in order to achieve a perfect social harmony...

verses.devanagari:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च |
रामो राज्यमुपासित्वा ब्रह्मलोकं गमिष्यति ||
verses.iast:
daśa varṣa sahasrāṇi daśa varṣa śatāni ca |
rāmo rājyam upāsitvā brahma lokam prayāsyati ||
verses.translation: "Having served the kingdom for ten thousand years and another one thousand years, i.e. for a total of eleven thousand years, Rama will go to the abode of Brahma...
notes: In rāmarājyam upāsitvā... the word used is upāsana is not ruling by sceptre but it is 'reverentially serving the kingdom...' as one would regard or treat his personal god with reverence. Rama thus served his kingdom as a devotee of his subjects and this is the concept of rāmarājya. The brahma loka is not the abode of four-faced Brahma, but still higher abode, rather VaikunTha itself.

glosses.meaning: having served the kingdom dasha-varSa-sahasraaNi = for ten thousand years
will go to the abode of Brahma.

verses.devanagari:
इदं पवित्रं पापघ्नं पुण्यं वेदैश्च सम्मितम् |
यः पठेद्रामचरितं सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ||
verses.iast:
idam pavitram pāpaghnam puṇyam vedaiḥ ca saṃmitam |
yaḥ paṭhet rāma caritam sarva pāpaiḥ pramucyate ||
verses.translation: "This Ramayana is holy, sin-eradicating, merit-endowing, and conformable with the teachings of Vedas. Whoever reads this Legend of Rama, will be verily liberated of all sins...

glosses.meaning: is truly liberated of all sins.

verses.devanagari:
एतदाख्यानमायुष्यं पठन् रामायणं नरः |
सपुत्रपौत्रः सगणः प्रेत्य स्वर्गे महीयते ||
verses.iast:
etat ākhyānam āyuṣyam paṭhan rāmāyaṇam naraḥ |
sa putra pautraḥ sa gaṇaḥ pretya svarge mahīyate ||
verses.translation: "This Ramayana is long-life giving. A narrative by reading which a human will be blessed with sons and grandsons, and after enjoying worldly comforts with attendants, will be adored in heaven after demise...

verses.devanagari:
पठन् द्विजो वागृषभत्वमीयात् |
स्यात् क्षत्रियो भूमिपतित्वमीयात् ||
वणिग्जनः पण्यफलत्वमीयात् |
जनश्च शूद्रोऽपि महत्त्वमीयात् ||
verses.iast:
paṭhan dvijo vāk ṛṣabhatvam īyāt |
syāt kṣatriyo bhūmi patitvam īyāt ||
vaṇik janaḥ paṇya phalatvam īyāt |
janaḥ ca śūdro api mahattvam īyāt ||
verses.translation: "By reading this Ramayana, that person if a Brahmana obtains excellency in speech, if a Kshatriya obtains land-lordship, if Vaisya attains profit in trade and even if a Sudra attains excellence." Thus Sage Narada gave a gist of Ramayana to Sage-poet Valmiki.
